title: Ledger posting consumer for transfer events
name: Ledger posting consumer

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this consumer guarantees that every transfer event is eventually posted to the ledger? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The same transfer event is delivered twice and both deliveries reach post() concurrently. What prevents a double posting?
choices: prefetch(20) ensures the two deliveries go to different consumers
The FOR UPDATE row locks on accounts
The ledger_postings insert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING: the second transaction blocks on the unique key, then sees rowCount 0 and commits without writing entries

questions.prompt: Why are the two account ids sorted before `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`?
choices: So that concurrent transfers A->B and B->A lock rows in the same order and cannot deadlock each other
So the debit is always applied before the credit
Postgres requires IN lists to be sorted
To make the ledger entries appear in sorted order

questions.prompt: What happens to a message whose amountMinor is 0?
choices: It is requeued and retried forever
It is rejected without requeue, so it is dropped or dead-lettered if the queue has a DLX configured
It is posted as a zero-value entry
It is acked and posted later
